title: Semantius locale file
description: One language, in the single shape every translation layer speaks: the repo catalogs under apps/web/src/locales, an operator's deployment file served from /locales/<code>.json, the tenant's ui_translations rows exported as a file, and translate mode's export. Which sections a file MAY carry depends on where it lives — a repo catalog carries messages, contexts and obsolete only (labels, server and rule are tenant or deployment data), which src/test/i18nCatalogs.test.ts enforces separately. The source string is the key: there are no message ids.

locale.description: The catalog language as a BCP-47 tag, e.g. de-DE. This is the language of the TEXT, never the formatting locale — those are two separate preferences.

name.description: The language's own name for itself ('Deutsch'). Wins over Intl.DisplayNames in the account menu, which is how a tag the browser has no display name for still reads as a language.

messages.description: Code strings, keyed by the English source text exactly as it appears in the app. An empty value means 'not translated yet' and falls through to the source text.

contexts.description: The same, for messages that carry a context because one English word has two meanings ('View' the noun, 'View' the verb). Keyed by context, then by source text.

labels.description: Model-label overrides. These are DATA — table, column, enum and module labels come from the semantic model, so no extractor can see them and they never appear in a repo catalog.

server.description: Messages the app cannot know in advance: PostgREST and RPC text raised by the backend. Looked up VERBATIM and never ICU-compiled, because server text may legitimately contain braces.

rule.description: Messages authored in the model's validation rules, looked up the same way as `server`.

obsolete.description: Translations whose source string no longer exists in the code. Repo catalogs only — written by `i18n:extract`, emptied by `i18n:extract --prune`.

enum.description: One entry per value of the column's enum, keyed by the stored value — never by its English label.
